description: THE GOAL IS TO BE THE BEST
summary: Mission Forge is an interactive space mission design game that runs in any web browser, including on a phone. Players choose a target (the Moon, Mars, asteroid Bennu, Europa, the James Webb Space Telescope or Titan), then design a complete mission. They pick a rocket, power source, antenna, ground station, science instruments, radiation shielding, orbit and mission length. Live bars show mass, power, budget and data, so every choice has a trade-off. Players then launch, face random events such as solar storms, and decide how to respond. A report explains why the mission succeeded or failed, gives a score and stars, shows a mission timeline, and compares the design to a real NASA mission such as LRO, MAVEN or Europa Clipper. The game has three levels, team play for up to four players, a daily challenge, a sandbox mode and a leaderboard. It makes real engineering trade-offs easy for students to learn by playing.
details:
Mission Forge is a browser game where players design a complete space mission. They choose a target (the Moon, Mars, asteroid Bennu, Europa, the James Webb Space Telescope or Titan), then pick a rocket, power source, antenna, ground station, instruments, radiation shielding, orbit and mission length. Live bars show mass, power, budget and data, and warnings explain what to fix. After launch, random events such as solar storms force the player to make a decision. A report then gives a score and stars, a mission timeline, and a comparison with a real NASA mission like LRO, MAVEN or Europa Clipper.
Benefits and impact: Students learn real engineering trade-offs by playing: a bigger rocket costs more, far targets get weak sunlight and slow communication, and radiation hurts science. It works on a phone with no install.
Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single file, with Claude as an AI assistant to help build and test it.
Creativity: It has three levels, team play for up to four players with different roles, a daily challenge, a sandbox mode, saved designs, an auto-design helper, and a leaderboard.
Factors considered: We balanced the game so every target can be won at every level and difficulty, kept the explanations simple for beginners, and based the mission facts on real NASA missions.
